transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

This is probably the hob's thermal protection kicking in. Induction hobs generate significant heat, and they have safety sensors that cut power to prevent damage if they get too hot. The most common reasons are blocked ventilation (e.g., pots touching the sides or debris in the vents) or a cooling fan that has stopped working. Please check for any obstructions around the hob's edges and listen to see if you hear a fan running when it is on high.
yeah the fan roars before it cuts out, louder than it used to be. no blockage round the edges that i can see. started after a new drawer unit went in under it last month

The louder roaring suggests the fan bearings are wearing out; a failing fan spins slower, causing the hob to overheat and cut out. We also need to rule out restricted airflow behind the unit. Please switch off and unplug the hob (or isolate it at the fuse), then try spinning the cooling fan by hand—usually found at the back of the appliance. Tell me if it feels stiff, gritty or wobbly.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
not doing that, im not going under the hob or pulling anything out. is there anything else it could be or do i need an engineer?

Given the louder roaring and your refusal to pull the hob out for inspection, this is likely a mechanical failure of the cooling fan itself. Since the hob is hard-wired into the mains and accessing the internal components requires dismantling the unit (which involves electrical safety risks), you will need an engineer to replace the fan or check for airflow restrictions behind the new drawer unit.
